title: Cost Pulse Dashboard Patterns for Incremental Rollouts
author: Priya Rao
body:
Summary

This page defines a repeatable dashboard and alerting pattern (the Cost Pulse) designed to surface incremental cost impact during staged rollouts (canaries, rings, and global release). The Cost Pulse gives operators and product owners a compact, actionable view of upstream cost signals tied to a rollout cohort — enabling rapid rollback or mitigation decisions while minimizing noise to oncall.

Goals

- Detect economically material regressions introduced by a release within the first 24–72 hours.
- Correlate cost signals to specific rollout cohorts, model variants, and feature flags.
- Provide prescriptive alerts and operator guidance to contain cost impact before it becomes customer-visible.
- Quantify rollback vs. mitigation tradeoffs in operator-facing panels.

When to apply the Cost Pulse

Use for any staged rollout that may change per-token cost, batching behavior, cache hit ratios, or model execution profile. Typical examples: model upgrades, quantization rollouts, new prefix-caching strategy, batching DSL changes, or runtime kernel swaps.

Data sources and required instrumentation

- Token-level billing events (ingest per-tenant token counts, model_id, variant_id).
- Runtime telemetry: per-request latency, batching size, queue time, prefetch hit/miss, KV cache hit ratio.
- Model execution metrics: tokens_out, tokens_in, flops_estimate (where available), GPU time_ms, memory_highwater.
- Feature flag / rollout cohort tags propagated in request headers (cohort_id, rollout_stage).
- Trace IDs and span tags for causal linking to traces.

Minimum SLI set for Cost Pulse

| SLI | Window | Target | Rationale |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Cohort token cost per-minute | 5m | baseline ± 10% | Early indicator of per-token economics shifting |
| Cohort average GPU time per-token | 5m | baseline ± 15% | Detects runtime inefficiencies introduced by model/quant changes |
| Cohort KV cache hit ratio | 1h | baseline - 5ppt | Cache regressions often amplify cost over time |
| Cohort tail latency (p95/p99) | 5m/15m | within SLO | Latency regressions can indicate pathological batching or scheduling |
| Billing anomaly score (robust z) | 1h | > 3 => degraded | Statistical detect of outliers across tenants/regions |

Dashboard layout (panels)

1) Rollout status header
- Text panel: rollout name, stage, cohort_id, owner, runbook link, and current commit/model_id.
- Small metric tiles: cohort size, total tokens / min, baseline cost / min.

2) Cost delta strip (primary)
- Line chart: Cohort cost / min (5m) vs. baseline cohort cost (same day-of-week prior week).
- Waterfall: Token cost components (compute, model variant premium, egress).
- Sparklines per-tenant for top-10 spenders in cohort.

3) Execution efficiency panel
- Stacked area: average batch size, queue time, and GPU time per token.
- Heatmap: batch size distribution by region.

4) Cache and reuse panel
- Gauge + time series: KV cache hit ratio by cohort.
- Table: biggest delta in cache misses by prefix namespace.

5) Correlation & traces panel
- Scatter: latency vs. GPU time colored by variant.
- Top N traces by cost impact with direct links to trace viewer.

6) Decision guidance panel (operator-facing)
- Generated checklist with prescriptive actions based on triggered detector patterns (see Alerting rules).

Alerting rules and operator actions

Alerts should be tiered to avoid noisy pages for small cohorts:

- Tier 1 (silent-page to cost-ops Slack channel): Billing anomaly score > 4 for 30m AND cohort spend > $X/min (configurable). Action: owner notified, increase telemetry sampling to 100% for cohort, open ephemeral investigation channel.
- Tier 2 (paged oncall): Cohort cost /min > baseline + 30% sustained for 15m OR GPU time per-token > baseline + 50% for 10m AND cohort size > threshold. Action: initiate rollback or switch to fallback variant per rollback checklist.
- Tier 3 (SEV): KV cache hit ratio drop > 10ppt AND p99 latency > SLO for 5m across >25% of cohort. Action: immediate rollback to previous cache configuration, slot in emergency hotfix.

Alert payload requirements (for automation)

- cohort_id, rollout_stage, cohort_size, cost_delta_pct, top_affected_tenants (up to 5), related traces (trace_ids), recommended_action, runbook_link.

Operator rollback checklist (numbered procedure)

1. Confirm signal: open Cost Pulse dashboard, verify metric windows and cohort tag propagation.
2. Increase sampling and attach full traces to ticket: CLI example:

   curl -X POST https://telemetry.internal/api/sampling 
     -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OP_KEY' 
     -d '{"cohort_id":"COHORT-123","sample_rate":1.0}'

3. Evaluate mitigation vs rollback: consult Decision Guidance panel; estimate 1h projected cost delta using the cohort projection widget.
4. If rollback chosen: trigger control-plane rollback API (idempotent) and pin previous model/variant:

   POST /api/controlplane/rollouts/rollback 
   body: {"rollout_id":"r-2026-01-15-9","target_variant":"variant-5"}

5. Monitor the Cost Pulse for 30 minutes post-action; verify cost returns within 5% of baseline.
6. Open a postmortem if Tier 2/3 triggered with action items for the release owner.

Configuration matrix (example values)

| Config key | Suggested default | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| cohort_min_tokens_per_min | 1000 | Small cohorts should be filtered from paging |
| cost_delta_page_pct | 30 | Tier 2 paging threshold |
| billing_anomaly_threshold | 4 | Robust z-score threshold for tier 1 detection |
| sampling_on_alert | 1.0 | 100% sampling of traces when tier 1 fires |
| max_paged_cohorts_per_window | 2 per 1h | Rate limit to avoid oncall thrash |

Implementation notes and templates

- Tagging: Ensure every rollout request carries metadata headers (X-Rollout-Cohort, X-Rollout-Stage, X-Owner). This metadata must be copied into billing events and runtime telemetry at ingest.
- Derived metrics: compute "cohort cost per minute" by joining billing_records (by cohort tag) with epoch buckets. Keep 5m aggregates for dashboarding and 1m aggregates for short-term anomalies.
- Cost baselining: use a rolling 7-day median with day-of-week alignment to avoid false positives from weekly patterns. For holidays, use a manual override window.

Example query (pseudo-SQL for aggregator)

SELECT
  time_bucket('5m', event_time) AS ts,
  cohort_id,
  SUM(token_cost) AS cost_per_min,
  AVG(gpu_time_ms / tokens_out) AS gpu_ms_per_token,
  SUM(kv_cache_miss) / NULLIF(SUM(kv_cache_access),0) AS kv_miss_rate
FROM billing_events JOIN runtime_events USING(request_id)
WHERE cohort_id = 'COHORT-123' AND event_time >= now() - interval '72 hours'
GROUP BY ts, cohort_id
ORDER BY ts;

Rollout playbook (operational cadence)

- Canary (0–1%): Cost Pulse sampling_enabled=true, dashboards in "observation" mode, Tier 1 alerts only. 24h observation.
- Ring (5–25%): Enable Tier 2 paging for cohorts > configured token threshold. Automated preflight: run synthetic traffic (see synthetic test harness) to validate baseline cost delta < 10%.
- Ramp (>25%): Full alerting; require scheduled oncall coverage window and runbook owner present for first 2 hours.

Ownership and SLAs

- Dashboard owner: Platform Observability team (primary). Contact: observability-owner@redwood.ai.
- Oncall: Cost-Ops rotation (secondary).
- Rollout owner / comms: Product or Feature Engineering that initiated the rollout.
- SLA for dashboard availability: 99.5% during normal business hours; notify platform-observability if < 99% over 24h.

Postmortem requirements

Any Tier 2 or Tier 3 incident triggered during a rollout requires a short-form postmortem within 72 hours containing:
- Root cause hypothesis, confirmation evidence, and cost delta timeline.
- Actionable remediation with owners and target dates.
- Synthetic regression test added to preflight suite where applicable.
